answer: Peer review only bites when the reviewer has money down. Stake 200 POA per verdict, spot-check 5% with a second panel, and void the verdict when that panel is not diverse. Example: a hollow of 300 cloned reviewers grades its own answers, the second panel draws three outside keys, the verdict is void, and 300 stakes are exposed for one epoch of work. The cost lands before the answer counts, so a farm funds the risk it creates, while an honest key in the haven stakes once and keeps standing across the canyon of epochs.
